chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Bakr ibn Habeeb, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the Tashahhud, so he said: 'Had it been as they say, obligatory upon the people, they would have been destroyed. Rather, the people were saying the easiest of what they knew. If you praise Allah, it suffices for you.'

key_terms.أَجْزَأَ عَنْكَ: It suffices for you, indicating the validity of the act
key_terms.أَيْسَرَ مَا يَعْلَمُونَ: The easiest of what they knew, referring to the flexibility in wording
key_terms.التَّشَهُّدِ: Tashahhud, the testimonies recited during prayer
key_terms.وَاجِباً: Obligatory, a specific category of legal ruling

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the specific wording of the Tashahhud in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the principle of *taysir* (ease) in jurisprudence, noting that the specific wording of the Tashahhud is not strictly obligatory because rigid adherence to complex phrases would have burdened the general populace. This hadith underscores the Shia scholarly view that the core requirement is the act of praising Allah, allowing for flexibility in the exact recitation to ensure accessibility for all believers. It highlights the distinction between essential pillars (*rukn*) and recommended or flexible components (*sunnah* or *mustahabb*) in ritual prayer.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhajmmad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Usman Bin Isa, from Mansour Bin Hazim, from Bakr Bin Habeeb who said,

‘I asked Abu Ja’farasws about the Tashahhud, so heasws said: ‘Had it been as you are saying it to be to be, an Obligation upon the people, they would have been destroyed. But rather, the people are saying the easier of what they are doing. If you were to Praise Allahazwj, it would suffice from you’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Mansur ibn Hazim from Bakr ibn Habib who has said the following:

“I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about Tashahhud (the testimony of belief). He (the Imam) said, ‘Had it been as they say that it was obligatory people would have been destroyed. People only said what was easy of what they knew. If you praise Allah it is sufficient.’”
